abstract: Array-agnostic enhancement networks generalize across microphone geometries but produce a single channel, while binaural enhancement methods preserve interaural cues only for one fixed device geometry. We propose BAmbiDrop, a framework that extends array-agnostic enhancement to binaural reproduction without retraining. Exploiting the fact that the Ambisonics origin is an arbitrary point in space, a frozen single-channel AmbiDrop network estimates a complex mask at multiple centers across the array; these masks are fused by a complex mean into a single shared mask, applied to the microphone signals and rendered by fixed BSM filters. Across 21 free-field and rigid-sphere arrays, the fused mask improves enhancement and interaural cue reproduction simultaneously, whereas masking each microphone independently degrades the latter without a consistent gain in the former.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对固定阵列双耳增强难泛化的问题，BAmbiDrop 把冻结的单通道 AmbiDrop 网络搬到每个麦克风对齐的 Ambisonics 原点上求掩码再平均成共享掩码，最后用固定 BSM 滤波器渲染双耳，在 21 种阵列平均上同时改善增强与空间线索，但绝对分数仍受 BSM 基准限制且依赖仿真条件。
originalTitle: BAmbiDrop: Array-Agnostic Speech Enhancement with Zero-Shot binaural Reproduction using Multi-center Ambisonics Encoding
readerTitle: BAmbiDrop：不换模型如何把任意麦克风阵列变成双耳增强输出
